doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Bernie Green and the albums 'Musically Mad' and 'More Than You Can Stand'
summary: Praise for Bernie Green, a decade at ABC, and the sidemen on the albums.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Tell me about Bernie Green. Sometimes he was Bernard Greenwald?

Bernard Green yes. He was a very good conductor, very good arranger. He knew what he wanted and he got it. He was a wonderful guy. He was a little excited sometimes but nice you know. And God, we worked together for about ten years at ABC.
His son told me that he used to say, “Al is the best.”
He said that about you. And you did that album called “Musically Mad” was it?
The “Mad” one, yeah. But the other one is “More Than You Can Stand.”

Yeah. Ray Crisara, trumpet, Charlie Margulis, and a great xylophonist and timpanist, George Gaber. He is one of the greatest timpanist/percussionists in the world. He went to Bloomington, Indiana, thirty years ago. And he’s still alive. He’s there. He’s one of the greatest. Things he could do with the timpanis you know, made different sounds. Yeah. George Gaber.
